title: The best café in town
subtitle: The newsletter survey — superlatives: the …-est, the most
canDo: I can say which is the best, the cheapest or the most popular.
I can understand the results of a survey.
I can give my opinion about places in my town.
teacherNotes: Türkçedeki "en" ve Arapçadaki "أفعل التفضيل" (الأكبر) İngilizcede the + -est / the most. Öğrenciler "the"yi sık unutur; tahtada the'yi kırmızıyla yuvarlak içine alın.
Anket sonuçlarını sınıfta gerçek bir ankete çevirin: "What's the best café / restaurant / park in your town?" Sonuçları tahtaya yazıp cümle kurdurun.
Karşılaştırma (-er) ile en üstünlük (-est) arasındaki farkı iki ve üç nesneyle gösterin: iki kalem → longer, üç kalem → the longest.

sections.title: Warm-up
prompts: What's the best café or restaurant in your town? Why?
Where do you go when you need a quiet place to study?
Do you answer surveys? What about?

items.example: We asked forty students in our survey.
Seventeen students voted for Sam's café.
And the winner is … Sam's café!
Forty percent of the students study at home.
The service is fast and friendly.
The Blue Cup has the fastest Wi-Fi.
It's the best café in town.
That was the worst coffee of my life!

sections.title: Listen and read
sections.heading: Just a little hint?
sections.scene: Thursday afternoon at Sam's café. Elif and Lucas have the survey results.

lines.speaker: sam
lines.text: So, what are the results? Is my café the best café on Harbor Street?

lines.speaker: elif
lines.text: Sorry, Sam, we can't tell you. The newsletter comes out tomorrow.

lines.speaker: sam
lines.text: Oh, come on. Just a little hint?

lines.speaker: lucas
lines.text: OK, a little one. Your cookies are the most popular cookies on the street.

lines.speaker: sam
lines.text: Of course they are. I make them with love.

lines.speaker: elif
lines.text: And your café is the coziest. People love the small tables. And Biscuit.

lines.speaker: lucas
lines.text: Well … Corner Coffee has the cheapest coffee. And The Blue Cup is the biggest and the quietest. A lot of students study there.

lines.speaker: sam
lines.text: The quietest? Hmm. My café isn't very quiet on Fridays, that's true. Your band is the loudest thing in here!

lines.speaker: elif
lines.text: But everyone says your service is the best. You're the friendliest owner on the street.

lines.speaker: sam
lines.text: Well, that's the most important thing. So who's the winner?

items.statement: The newsletter comes out on Friday.

sections.title: Read
sections.heading: The best café on Harbor Street
sections.intro: The survey results in the school newsletter, by Elif Kaya and Lucas Silva.
paragraphs: Last month, we asked forty students one question: what's the best café on Harbor Street? Here are the results.
Corner Coffee is the cheapest café on the street. A coffee is only $1.75, and it opens the earliest, at six in the morning.
But it's also the smallest: there are only four tables. Twelve students voted for it.
The Blue Cup is the biggest and the most modern café. It has the fastest Wi-Fi and the most comfortable chairs.
It's also the quietest, so it's the best place to study. Eleven students voted for it.
And the winner is … Sam's café! Seventeen students voted for Sam's: that's more than forty percent.
It isn't the cheapest or the biggest café, but it's the coziest, and the service is the friendliest.
And the cookies? "The best cookies in Boston," one student wrote. "The worst thing about Sam's café? It's closed on Sundays!"

sections.title: Grammar: superlatives
look: The Blue Cup has **the most comfortable** chairs.
rules: Use **the** before a superlative: *the biggest*, *the most popular*.
After a superlative, we often use **in** + a place: *the best café **in** Boston*.
examples: January is the coldest month in Boston.
Mount Everest is the highest mountain in the world.
What's the most beautiful city in your country?
This is the worst coffee in town!

support.tr: En üstünlük (en): kısa sıfatlar the + -est alır (cheap → the cheapest = en ucuz), uzun sıfatlar the most alır (the most popular = en popüler). Türkçedeki "en"in karşılığı the …-est veya the most'tur; the unutulmaz. Düzensizler: good → the best, bad → the worst. "…'deki en …" için çoğunlukla in kullanılır: the best café in Boston = Boston'daki en iyi kafe.
support.ar: التفضيل: الصفات القصيرة تأخذ the + ‎-est‎ (cheap → the cheapest = الأرخص)، والطويلة تأخذ the most (the most popular = الأكثر شعبية). يشبه «الأفعل» في العربية (الأكبر، الأرخص)، ولا ننسى the. الشاذة: good → the best، bad → the worst. وبعدها نستخدم in مع المكان: the best café in Boston = أفضل مقهى في بوسطن.

wrong: Sam's café is best café in town.
right: Sam's café is the best café in town.

ar.note: لا نجمع most مع ‎-est‎، ونستخدم in مع الأماكن.
wrong: He's the best student of our class.
right: He's the best student in our class.

sections.title: Write: The best place in my town

model.heading: The best falafel in Amman — Omar
text: The best place to eat in Amman? For me, it's a small falafel shop near my old school.
It isn't the biggest or the most modern restaurant in the city. There are only three tables.
But the falafel is the freshest and the cheapest in town: a sandwich is less than one dollar.
The owner is the friendliest man in our neighborhood. He knows everybody's name.
My favorite time to go there is Friday morning, before the shop gets crowded.
